units.translation: needing purification, a suppliant. A. Ixion
receiving the gifts of the gods from a pure man
and take care of the sacred public rites
the rites of the fireless sacrifices

sacred. [The Ionic form ἱρός [sacred] the tragedians sometimes used not only in lyric passages when the meter demanded it, but also in dialogue to avoid a tribrach. This form in Sophocles OC 16 χῶρος δ᾽ ὅδ᾽ ἱρὸς, ὡς ἀπεικάσαι, βρύων [this place is sacred, as one may guess, teeming], the Laurentian manuscript preserves, with Suidas agreeing under the word Ιρος [sacred], whence at line 54, where the manuscript has χῶρος μὲν ἱερός [the place is sacred], and in many other places of the tragedians (two in Aeschylus, Sept. 268 and fr. 19) it should be restored, where the poets wrote ἱρός [sacred] preferring the disyllabic foot to the trisyllabic (just as for the same reason they used the apocope of the preposition ἀνά [up] in verbs compounded with it), and it was expelled by copyists with almost the same consistency with which they removed that apocope, not even excepting those places where the manifest law of meter excludes the trisyllabic form ἱερός [sacred], about which I have spoken in the Thesaurus vol. 4 p. 544. One must be careful, however, not to go too far and claim that the tragedians also used the Ionic form of ἱερεύς [priest] and of nouns compounded with ἱερός [sacred], all of which were less frequently used, either in the middle of verses or, what is even less probable, in the first foot of the trimeter, as in Aeschylus fr. 326 (if Casaubon conjectured correctly) iεράν τε Βούραν [and sacred Bura] – and in Sophocles OR 18 ἱερῆς, ἐγὼ μὲν Ζηνὸς, οἱ δ᾽ ἐπ᾿ ἠθέων [of the sacred, I am of Zeus, but they are by the shores], where no one will easily persuade himself that Aeschylus and Sophocles, to avoid an anapest which they admitted in so many other places, had recourse to the Ionic forms ἱράν [sacred] (which would be a mixture of ἱρήν [sacred] and ἱεράν [sacred]) and ἱρῆς [sacred]. By a similar rule the use of the words ἱκετὴρ ἱκτήρ [suppliant], ἱκέτης ἵκτης [suppliant], ἱκέτις ἵκτις [suppliant woman], ἱκετήριος ἱκτήριος [suppliant] is governed, which are said with the letter e either preserved or elided, about which I have explained in the Oxford annotation on Sophocles OR 185.]
where Casaubon rightly has ἱεράν τε Βούραν [and sacred Bura], unless one prefers Meineke's conjecture (Vindic. Strabon. p. 127) Βούραν καθ᾽ ἱεράν [Bura down through the sacred land].
the sacred stream of the sea
the sacred speaking timber of Argos
and sacred Bura and the thunder-struck Rhypes
this place is sacred, as one may guess, teeming
of the sacred, I am of Zeus, but they are by the shores
Bura down through the sacred land
confidence, easily persuaded, sits on the dear throne of the mind
and may the swarm of diseases from the citizens sit upon the head, joyless
I will seat you on the sheaves
he seats this fourth prophet on the throne
